title: Radiometric Dating
description: A radioactive parent decays at a fixed rate into its daughter, so the ratio of daughter to parent in a rock or a bone is a clock that started when it formed. Carbon-14 dates bones tens of thousands of years old; potassium-40 dates the ash beds around fossils hundreds of millions of years old; rubidium-87 dates the oldest rocks of all. Unlocks the Dating Spectrometer.

puzzle.goal: A sample formed with parent atoms only; each decay turns one parent into a daughter, with mean life τ. Count the daughters D and the parents P left, and write t, the time since it formed.
puzzle.name: The age equation
puzzle.ask: Find t in years for a basalt: τ = @{tau} years, D/P from D = @{D} and P = @{P} atoms.
puzzle.method: P = P₀e^(−t/τ) and D = P₀ − P, so P₀/P = 1 + D/P: take the logarithm.
